note: Alternate picking with three notes a string, so each string starts on the other stroke. The picking-drill sounds its own metronome, so no backing-band sits beside it; the text is about pick strokes, which is the only row the drill has. The why is the mechanism (an odd number of notes flips the stroke at each string), the feel to reach starts "Practice until" and names muscle memory, and the tempo is moves (80 to 120 bpm), named only as a param.

exercise.title: Alternate picking, three notes a string
exercise.why: With three notes on a string the strokes go down, up, down, so the next string starts on an up stroke, and the hand learns to cross strings on either stroke without breaking its down-up swing.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. The drill plays with it, one note per beat, and the note playing is lit on the tab.
Pick three notes on each open string, starting on the low E string, up to the high e string and back down. Follow the arrows under the tab, down and up without a break, even where the string changes.
Practice until the strokes are in your muscle memory: your hand keeps its down-up swing through every string change without you thinking.
